title: Visual Pegs & Picture Links
subtitle: Turn boring numbers into unforgettable picture stories!

sections.prompt: Can you memorize this random 4-item grocery list in 15 seconds: Apples, Milk, Bread, Honey?
sections.subtext: Try creating an image in your mind before we show you the peg secret!

panels.text: Aarav keeps forgetting lists and pin codes. Numbers look like dry black ink on white paper.
Professor Piko says: 'Your brain thinks in pictures, not numbers! Look at the number 2—what does it look like? A graceful Swan!'
2 is a Swan 🦢, 5 is a Hand ✋ (5 fingers), 7 is a sharp Axe 🪓, and 8 is a Snowman ⛄!
If I need to remember item #2 is Milk, I picture a Swan swimming in a lake of cold Milk! It's so silly I can never forget it!
BEEP! Picture power activated! Let's connect numbers to pegs in the simulation!

sections.title: The Number-Shape Peg System
sections.summary: Attach each number to a vivid object shaped like the number. When you see the number, the picture pops up!

interactions: Drag each number to its matching picture peg shape
Link the peg to the item to lock it into memory
config.completionCondition: All 4 number pegs correctly linked to their visual objects

questions.prompt: In the Number-Shape peg system, why does the number 2 represent a Swan 🦢?

options.label: Because the curved neck of a swan looks just like the curve of a 2

hints: Look at the shape of the digit 2 and the shape of a swan's neck.

questions.prompt: You need to remember code 8-2. What mental movie creates the strongest visual memory?

options.label: A Snowman ⛄ riding on the back of a giant Swan 🦢
Writing 8 and 2 on a piece of paper
Repeating 'eight two eight two' ten times

hints: Remember: vivid, colorful, silly interactions stick forever!
